extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) before the USPTO and USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order setting forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions in a USPTO disciplinary proceeding under 35 U.S.C. and 37 C.F.R.; describes violations, required actions, reinstatement criteria, publication/notification, and OED procedures. Targeted at regulated practitioners and enforcement staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(1) — violating a Disciplinary Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges conduct violated Rule 10.23(b)(1) by violating a Disciplinary Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounded on stipulated facts and the Louisiana Supreme Court order accepting a joint petition for consent discipline; used as a basis for USPTO discipline in settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent engaged in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation in violation of Rule 10.23(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative factual basis: representing a client in a jurisdiction where not licensed, arranging for another attorney to handle the matter while taking a substantially larger net fee, and failing to declare the fee on Federal and State income tax returns. Such misconduct supports disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) — conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent engaged in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice, in violation of Rule 10.23(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where respondent's actions undermine public confidence or proper functioning of legal processes; alleged misconduct in state disciplinary proceeding formed predicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice before the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent engaged in conduct that adversely reflects on his fitness to practice before the USPTO, violating Rule 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used where conduct calls into question an individual's competence, trustworthiness, or suitability to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) — suspension by state authority on ethical grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was suspended from practice as an attorney on ethical grounds by a duly constituted state authority, in violation of Rule 10.23(c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state suspension on ethical grounds is itself a basis for USPTO disciplinary action; here predicated on the June 18, 2010 Louisiana Supreme Court order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: Twelve-month suspension from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for a period of twelve (12) months from the practice of patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO commencing thirty days from the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent eligible to request reinstatement after serving six (6) months of the 12-month suspension (see reinstatement petition rules below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition granted for narrow purpose and limited time
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date the Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after that date, solely to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is temporary and restricted to client-notification-related tasks under the cited regulation; expires automatically after 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (client notification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the client-notification obligations of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Client notification duties (referred to in the order) must be performed and are tied to limited recognition and reinstatement; meeting § 11.58 obligations also satisfies certain notification provisions under § 11.20(a)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated; respondent may not obtain such credentials until reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition showing requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c) and § 11.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reinstatement to practice before the USPTO will be granted only upon petition showing: (1) good moral character and reputation, competency, and learning in law required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.7; (2) resumption will not be detrimental to the administration of justice or subversive to the public interest; (3) full compliance with the Final Order; and (4) full compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the substantive evidentiary thresholds the OED Director requires before recommending reinstatement to the USPTO Director or designee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing petition for reinstatement (early petition provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time after seven (7) months from the date the Final Order is signed, respondent may file a petition for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 requesting reinstatement effective prior to the expiration of the 12-month suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if an early reinstatement petition is filed, the OED Director must be satisfied with the statutory reinstatement criteria; the petition may lead to staying remaining suspension if granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and treatment of 'remaining period of suspension' and stay mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Remaining period of suspension' means the initial twelve (12) month suspension minus the period from thirty days after the Final Order is signed until reinstatement; if not reinstated after 12 months, there is no remaining period. The OED Director shall stay any remaining suspension period if a petition requesting immediate reinstatement is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how time served and early reinstatement affect any suspended residual period and how stays are administratively handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation upon reinstatement (24-month probationary period)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon reinstatement, respondent shall serve a twenty-four (24) month probationary period, beginning upon reinstatement, during which respondent shall be permitted to practice before the USPTO unless the stay of the suspension is lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation conditions are enforceable; misconduct during probation can trigger lifting the stay and immediate suspension to serve the remaining suspension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director Order to Show Cause procedure for probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED Director believes respondent failed to comply during probation, the OED Director shall: (A) issue an Order to Show Cause why the stay should not be lifted and respondent immediately suspended for all/part of remaining suspension; (B) send the Order to Show Cause to respondent at last address of record; and (C) grant respondent fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If after the 15-day response period the OED Director remains of that opinion, the Director will compile and transmit the Order to Show Cause, respondent's response (if any), and evidence to the USPTO Director or designee requesting an order lifting the stay and suspending respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and actions if suspension is made executory
rubrics_metrics.description: If the stay is lifted and suspension made executory, respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; OED shall disseminate information per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; USPTO shall dissociate respondent's name from customer numbers and PKI certificates; respondent may not use or obtain such credentials until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the administrative and public-notice steps that follow an executory suspension, including dissociation and publication duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: No stay of Director's order by seeking review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director or designee enters an order lifting the stay and suspending respondent and respondent seeks review of that action, such review shall not operate to postpone or hold in abeyance the Director's order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative review does not automatically delay the effect of the Director's suspension order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.59 and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and shall publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette; under § 11.59 the OED Director shall notify disciplinary agencies in states where respondent is admitted, courts where known admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public dissemination of discipline is mandatory per cited regulations and includes an Official Gazette notice describing violations and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client-notification compliance satisfies § 11.20(a)(4) notification provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 regarding client notification satisfy the notification provisions set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.20(a)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fulfills cross-referenced regulatory notification requirements when client notice obligations under § 11.58 are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishment and restitution obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall relinquish his entire fee collected in the underlying matter and make full restitution, with interest, to the complainants, in accordance with the Louisiana order accepted June 18, 2010, and related documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must comply with state-imposed restitution/relinquishment terms; upon requesting reinstatement respondent must provide corroborating evidence of compliance with these obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax-related compliance reporting during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: During the probationary period (as imposed by the Louisiana order), respondent is required to provide the Louisiana Office of the Disciplinary Counsel with copies of his personal tax returns with all appropriate schedules to ensure compliance with relevant tax filing requirements; upon requesting reinstatement, respondent shall provide OED with corroborating evidence of such compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax filing transparency during probation is a condition tied to discipline and to demonstrating rehabilitation for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record use in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, shall be considered when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct and/or in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor and/or to rebut any statement or representation by or on respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The existence of this order may increase severity of future discipline or undermine claims of mitigation or rehabilitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that, under this settlement, each side pays its own costs (contrasted with other orders that may require respondent to pay investigation or disciplinary costs).
